summary.oneLiner: Premier is the only Indian firm qualified to manufacture countermeasures (chaffs/flares) and a rare exporter of fully assembled rocket motors. Highest-ever order book of INR1,569 cr (4.04x FY26 revenue) gives 2–3 year visibility. FY26 revenue de-grew (high base of FY25 emergency chaffs/flares orders + raw-material/execution disruptions from two plant accidents), but margins recovered sharply on better mix and pricing. FY27 thesis hinges on re-acceleration as the accident-hit flares plant is recommissioned, alternate raw materials get DRDO clearance, and new verticals (land mines, drone/loitering-munition payloads, medium-caliber ammunition) ramp.

scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | FY26 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR89.2 cr | +20% | INR388.3 cr | −7% |
| EBIT | INR9.6 cr | +35% | INR69.3 cr | +42% |
| EBIT margin | 10.8% | — | 17.8% | — |
| Net profit (PAT) | INR6.6 cr | +78% | INR45.8 cr | +61% |
| PAT margin | 7.4% | — | 11.8% | — |
| Defence & Space rev (Q4) | INR67.7 cr (76% of mix) | +43% | — | — |
| Order book | INR1,569 cr (4.04x FY26 rev) | highest ever | — | — |
| Other income | INR13 cr | one-off | INR42 cr | one-off |
guidance:
- **FY27 revenue: INR600–700 cr** (~55–80% growth on FY26's INR388 cr); margin **15–20%**.
- Export contribution in FY27 ~INR200 cr; domestic ~INR500 cr. Quarterly skew expected (inspection/dispatch and import timing).
- Mgmt conceded prior Feb-26 call guidance of ~INR500 cr for FY26 was missed (came in ~INR390 cr). Analysts repeatedly flagged the INR600–700 cr target as aggressive given execution track record; mgmt defends it via the large order book ("run rate is achievable").
order book:
- INR1,569 cr total (highest ever): Defence INR1,491 cr (95%), Explosives INR31 cr (2%), Services/O&M INR47 cr (3%).
- Export ~54% / domestic ~46%. Of ~INR800 cr export orders: >INR400 cr in development stage (milestone-based invoicing), ~INR400 cr awaiting export licences.
- Mgmt expects book to stay at ~INR1,000 cr+ even as it executes, given pipeline + new capacities.
- New **INR350.23 cr export order** (April 2026) for defence products to international clients; export licence expected in ~3 months.
- Oct-2025 INR430 cr order: execution just started; ~2/3 expected in FY27, 1/3 spilling to FY28.
- A INR18.9 cr order (won Feb-26) was **cancelled in April** because export licence was not granted — illustrates licence risk on the book.
segment:
- **Defence & Space** = 76% of Q4 revenue (INR67.7 cr, +43% YoY) — the growth engine. Products: chaffs/flares, rocket motors (incl. fully assembled for export), warheads, mines, ammunition, solid propellants (MRSAM, LRSAM, Astra), pyrogen igniters.
- **Industrial Explosives**: small, raw-material-constrained.
- **Services/O&M**: ISRO propellant service contract ~INR18 cr/yr, ~2.5 years remaining (to ~H2 FY29), roughly constant. **Lost Jagdalpur (Agni missile propellant) O&M contract** on a competitive bid (cost too high) — but still single-source to DRDO for plant-made items.
growth drivers:
- Re-execution of FY25-delayed orders (flares, mines) now that the Peddakandukur flares plant is recommissioned and in-house flare/component production restored (cuts import dependence).
- New verticals: land mines, drone/loitering-munition payloads, medium-caliber ammunition — demand boosted by recent global conflicts; DRDO now accepting in-house alternate raw material (vs MIL shortfall).
- Defence exports (fully assembled rocket motors, warheads); chaffs/flares fresh RFPs/negotiations underway.
- Optionality: QRSAM order (not in current estimates/book), potential rocket-motor full-build for domestic missiles if opportunity arises.
- New capacity: Katepally RDX/HMX + planetary mixer expansion; new AP 400-acre defence facility; Odisha (phase 2/3, 4–5 yrs out).
margins:
- FY26 EBIT margin 17.8% (EBIT +42% despite −7% revenue) — strong mix/pricing. Q4 EBIT margin lower at 10.8%.
- FY26 was hit by **elevated raw-material prices** amid global tensions (industry-wide). PAT helped by one-off other income (vendor discounts/negotiated settlements on delayed deliveries — explicitly non-recurring; INR13 cr Q4 / INR42 cr FY26).
- FY27 margin guide 15–20% — implies normalization, no further one-off other-income tailwind.
capex:
- FY26 capex ~INR28 cr. Total FY26+FY27 program ~INR60 cr; **FY27 capex ~INR32 cr** (INR60−28).
- PDK flares plant already capitalised/productionised in FY25; balance = new mixers, storage magazines.
- Katepally RDX/HMX expansion + large planetary mixer ongoing; some capitalisation by Q1 FY27, full commissioning may slip to Q3 FY27 (plant + product qualification adds 1–2 months).
- Katepally large-rocket-motor line (accident-hit) rebuild: commissioning ~September 2026, production from ~November 2026.
capital allocation:
- Funding internal capex (~INR32 cr FY27) plus pursuing 400-acre AP land (price negotiation ongoing with AP govt at Secretary level — seeking discount). Odisha land deferred (4–5 yrs). No buyback/dividend/leverage commentary in this call.
- Active JV with NIBE (global ammunition) + multiple strategic MoUs with drone makers for payload supply.
risks:
- **Execution risk** (repeatedly flagged): two FY25 plant accidents (Katepally large rocket motors; Peddakandukur flares), import/shipping delays from geopolitics, free-issue-material (FIM) dependence from BDL/DRDO gating domestic deliveries (~40–50 motors/month limited by FIM availability).
- **Export-licence risk** — under Arms Act, govt/country-policy dependent; INR18.9 cr order cancelled in April for this reason; ~INR400 cr of book awaiting licences.
- Raw-material availability (MIL shortfall on high explosives for land mines) — partially mitigated via DRDO-accepted alternate material still in trials (1–2 months to clearance).
- Aggressive FY27 guidance vs weak FY26 delivery; lumpy quarterly revenue; pending ~INR30 cr LD reversal claim with MoD (uncertain recovery).
mgmt tone: Confident but candid. Openly acknowledged FY26 guidance miss and execution problems; frames FY27 target as "we'll try our best… run-rate achievable." Emphasizes structural defence tailwinds and unique countermeasures/rocket-motor positioning. Tempered optimism, not promotional.
non-obvious points:
- Only Indian firm qualified for countermeasures; sole source of flares to IAF — backward integration now reduces import dependence.
- FY27 export guide (INR200 cr) is largely **development orders**; once productionised, follow-on production orders are "a little larger" — embedded upside if conversion happens.
- Mgmt sees a structural moat: a new entrant needs ~5 years minimum to establish an explosives unit/storage, despite consolidation and new AP-region entrants.
- Lost the Agni-missile Jagdalpur O&M contract on price — a reminder that O&M is competitively bid and not sticky.
- Not pursuing full rocket-motor build for domestic missiles (no electronics/seekers/guidance); only for exports — caps domestic content per missile.
- ~INR30 cr LD reversal claim pending; mgmt "always claims the largest amount" — recovery uncertain, potential one-off upside.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge / theme | Direction | Name | NSE | BSE | Role | Conviction | Covered | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Defence indigenization / countermeasures & rocket-motor exports | Beneficiary | Premier Explosives | PREMEXPLN | 526247 | Sole Indian countermeasures maker; rocket-motor & warhead exporter | High | self | INR1,569 cr book, 4.04x rev; FY27 guide INR600–700 cr |
| Raw-material (high-explosive) supply shortfall for land mines | Loser | Munitions India Ltd (MIL) | (unlisted) | (code unverified) | Sole HE supplier that failed to meet PREMEXPLN demand; being substituted in-house | Med | external | Lost share as PREMEXPLN develops DRDO-accepted alternate material |
| Agni-missile propellant O&M (Jagdalpur) re-bid | Loser | Premier Explosives | PREMEXPLN | 526247 | Incumbent O&M provider; lost contract on price | Med | self | Cost rose; new contractor won; still single-source to DRDO for plant items |
| Drone / loitering-munition payload demand | Beneficiary | Premier Explosives | PREMEXPLN | 526247 | Payload supplier via MoUs to multiple drone OEMs | Med | self | New vertical; ramp pending alt-RM clearance |
| Free-issue-material dependence (FIM) gating domestic deliveries | Beneficiary | BDL (Bharat Dynamics) | BDL | 543958 | Customer/FIM provider for missile motors (LRSAM/MRSAM/Astra) | Med | external | (code unverified) PREMEXPLN delivery paced by BDL/DRDO FIM supply |
| ISRO launch-cadence increase → propellant demand | Beneficiary | Premier Explosives | PREMEXPLN | 526247 | ISRO propellant service ~INR18 cr/yr, 2.5 yrs left; will re-bid | Med | self | Constant run-rate; renewal RFP after current term |

- **Guidance reset:** Prior Feb-26 call implied ~INR500 cr FY26; actual ~INR388 cr (miss). New FY27 guide INR600–700 cr at 15–20% margin.
- **Order book at record high** INR1,569 cr (vs prior commentary); + new INR350.23 cr export order (Apr-26).
- **Accident recovery progress:** Peddakandukur flares plant recommissioned and in regular in-house production (was down ~1.5 yrs); Katepally large-rocket-motor line rebuild commissioning ~Sep-26, production ~Nov-26.
- **Raw material:** DRDO now accepting in-house alternate material (vs earlier refusal); trials ongoing, clearance expected 1–2 months — unlocks land-mine/ammo orders.
- **New negatives surfaced:** INR18.9 cr order cancelled (Apr-26) on export-licence denial; Jagdalpur Agni O&M contract lost on re-bid.
- **One-off other income** INR13 cr (Q4) / INR42 cr (FY26) flagged as non-recurring (vendor discounts) — won't repeat.

themes.title: Defence indigenization & order-book visibility
themes.need: Indigenization mandates (IDDM / Atmanirbhar / DcPP) plus multi-year order books make domestic defence the cleanest revenue-conversion theme - across electronics, drones, simulators, explosives/munitions and precision systems. BEL guides >INR55k cr FY27 inflow (~INR30k cr QRSAM pending CCS clearance, guided by September) on a INR72,258cr order book; HAL book ~INR2.55 lakh cr; SOLARINDS defence revenue +94% to INR2,634cr FY26, guided >INR4,500cr FY27 on an ~INR18,000cr defence order book (Bhargavastra counter-drone trials completing CY2026); DATAPATTNS inflows strong; BHARATFORG/BEML add land-systems and platforms.
themes.driver: Backlog-to-revenue conversion underway; BEL's QRSAM CCS clearance (guided by Sep-2026, ~INR30k cr of the FY27 inflow guide) is the load-bearing near-term catalyst; fresh MoD orders + emergency procurement; HAL LCA Mk-1A ramp (gated on GE engines).

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Claims a set of firsts: "1st in India to manufacture Explosives and Detonating fuse with indigenous technology", "1st in the World to produce Safer and Greener NHN detonators on commercial scale", and "1st Private Company to manufacture Solid Propellants to missile programs".
- States it is "the only qualified Indian company for countermeasures and also specializes in the export of fully assembled rocket motors", and the "Only domestic manufacturer and supplier" of counter-measures to Indian Defence.
- Entry barriers framed as licences for manufacturing high energy products from DPIIT and PESO, participation in defence and space programmes with indigenous technology and technology transfer, and DSIR-certified / NABL-accredited laboratories.
- Runs O&M of the solid propellant plant of ISRO at SHAR since 2006 and of Advanced Systems Laboratory (ASL) at the Solid Fuel Complex, Jagdalpur for 17 years — a long-dated services annuity alongside manufacturing.
- Supplies 100% of solid propellant requirements for MRSAM, LRSAM and Astra; pyrogen igniters for all stages of Agni; production and integration of rocket motors for Brahmos; and has supplied 2,500+ booster grains and 450+ sustainer grains for Akash.

- FY27 export guide (INR200 cr) is largely **development orders**; once productionised, follow-on production orders are "a little larger" — embedded upside if conversion happens.
- Mgmt sees a structural moat: a new entrant needs ~5 years minimum to establish an explosives unit/storage, despite consolidation and new AP-region entrants.
- Lost the Agni-missile Jagdalpur O&M contract on price — a reminder that O&M is competitively bid and not sticky.
- Not pursuing full rocket-motor build for domestic missiles (no electronics/seekers/guidance); only for exports — caps domestic content per missile.
- ~INR30 cr LD reversal claim pending; mgmt "always claims the largest amount" — recovery uncertain, potential one-off upside.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge / theme | Direction | Name | Role | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Defence indigenization / countermeasures & rocket-motor exports | Beneficiary | Premier Explosives (PREMEXPLN) | Sole Indian countermeasures maker; rocket-motor & warhead exporter | High | INR1,569 cr book, 4.04x rev; FY27 guide INR600–700 cr |
| Raw-material (high-explosive) supply shortfall for land mines | Loser | Munitions India Ltd (MIL) | Sole HE supplier that failed to meet PREMEXPLN demand; being substituted in-house | Med | Lost share as PREMEXPLN develops DRDO-accepted alternate material |

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body:
- **Guidance reset:** Prior Feb-26 call implied ~INR500 cr FY26; actual ~INR388 cr (miss). New FY27 guide INR600–700 cr at 15–20% margin.
- **Order book at record high** INR1,569 cr (vs prior commentary); + new INR350.23 cr export order (Apr-26).
- **Accident recovery progress:** Peddakandukur flares plant recommissioned and in regular in-house production (was down ~1.5 yrs); Katepally large-rocket-motor line rebuild commissioning ~Sep-26, production ~Nov-26.
- **Raw material:** DRDO now accepting in-house alternate material (vs earlier refusal); trials ongoing, clearance expected 1–2 months — unlocks land-mine/ammo orders.
- **New negatives surfaced:** INR18.9 cr order cancelled (Apr-26) on export-licence denial; Jagdalpur Agni O&M contract lost on re-bid.
- **One-off other income** INR13 cr (Q4) / INR42 cr (FY26) flagged as non-recurring (vendor discounts) — won't repeat.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Change of control] Apollo Micro Systems is acquiring a 41.33% promoter stake in Premier Explosives for ~Rs 1,550 Cr, all cash, with expected closure in Q3FY27 (Dec'26, subject to approvals).
- [Open offer] An open offer to acquire a 26% stake (1.40 Cr shares) at Rs 698 per share, aggregating Rs 976 Cr.
- [Post-deal platform] The combined entity is presented as spanning defence electronics (Apollo) plus energetic materials, rocket motors, ammunition & countermeasures and aerospace systems, with claimed benefits of broader customer base, supply chain resilience and ability to win larger, complex programmes.
- [Demand backdrop] Deck cites a Rs 6,81,000 Cr FY26 defence budget with Rs 1,80,000 Cr capital outlay, defence production of ~Rs 1,50,000 Cr (FY25) targeting Rs 3,00,000 Cr by FY29, exports of Rs 23,622 Cr (FY25) targeting Rs 50,000 Cr by 2029, Rs 2,09,050 Cr of contracts signed in FY25 with ~89% sourced domestically, and 5 positive indigenisation lists covering 5,500+ items under import embargo.
- [Near-term execution risk] Management attributes the Q1FY27 revenue decline to "delays in dispatches and project execution amid ongoing global headwinds and supply chain disruptions" and margin pressure to "elevated raw material prices", stating execution momentum will improve in coming quarters.
